subjects.supportFinding: Supports the path-k mechanism as asserted: (d)(1) enumerates the eligible convictions (§§ 3503, 5503, 5506, 5507, 5902, and simple possession of a controlled substance) committed as a direct result of being a trafficking victim; (d)(2)(ii) requires consent by the attorney for the Commonwealth; (d)(2)(iii)-(iv) and (e) set the evidentiary requirements and the official-documentation presumption; (f) sets the grant standard; (g) mandates vacatur, striking of the adjudication of guilt, and expungement of all related records. E must still compare the compiled pathway's eligible-offense list, consent handling and participant treatment against this enumerated scope — the statute's offense list is closed, not general.

operatorConfirmation.confirmedBy: Roger (project owner), via independent web-capable research relayed to this lane 2026-08-11
operatorConfirmation.finding: Current S.C. Code § 16-3-2020(F) expressly permits a trafficking victim to move to expunge a conviction or delinquency adjudication for specified nonviolent misdemeanor or Class F felony offenses committed as a direct result of, or interrelated to, trafficking; preponderance standard; reasonable notice to the original prosecuting agency and affected victims. An expungement mechanism under current law, not merely an offense statute.
operatorConfirmation.standing: Operator-supplied substantive confirmation. Resolves the offense-only-versus-relief question and re-scopes this blocker to byte transfer only. NOT final authority for the receipt: the receipt's verified authority, operative span, currentness (including the 2024 amendment and editor's note) and support verdict fill only from the served official bytes.

subjects.recommendedE3Disposition: proceed — official text is preserved and receipted; adjudicate the relationship on the pinned bytes. SC: the registry-gap analysis can now be completed against a proven expungement mechanism, including 2024 retroactivity.
subjects.supportFinding: Relief classification from the bytes: EXPUNGEMENT — (F) grants a motion-based expungement remedy (not vacatur, sealing, or an offense-only provision): a trafficking victim convicted or adjudicated delinquent of a violation of the trafficking article, prostitution, or any other nonviolent misdemeanor or Class F felony (defined by reference to § 16-1-20(A)(6)-(9)) may motion to expunge; grant standard is preponderance that participation was a direct result of or interrelated to being a victim; reasonable notice to the original prosecuting agency and to victims per the Victim's Bill of Rights is required. (F) also carries a distinct affirmative-defense clause for prosecutions — E should treat the defense and the expungement remedy as separate operative effects of the same subsection.
